stemMd: A ramp rises 1 m for every √3 m of horizontal run. What is its angle above the horizontal?
explanationMd: The tangent of the angle is rise divided by horizontal run, 1/√3. This is tan30°. The angle is less than forty-five degrees because the rise is smaller than the run.

distractorRationale.c: This uses the reciprocal of the rise-to-run ratio.
distractorRationale.e: That would require equal rise and run.
distractorRationale.d: A vertical ramp would have zero horizontal run.
distractorRationale.a: Its tangent is not one over square root of three.
